AIRFLOA RAIL TECHNOLOGY : RECEIVES INTERIM STAY FROM MADRAS HIGH COURT

• The Hon'ble High Court of Judicature at Madras granted an interim stay on adjudication orders imposing penalties under Section 135(7) of the Companies Act, 2013.
• The stay is conditional upon the company paying 50% of the penalty amount imposed by the Registrar of Companies within twelve weeks.
• The matter pertains to delay in transferring CSR obligations for FY 2019-20, 2020-21, 2021-22 and 2022-23.
• The total penalty imposed by ROC was ₹1,05,42,290.00, with the company's share being ₹90,03,968.00 and directors' ₹15,38,322.00.
• The penalty on the company was enhanced by the Regional Director in appeal.
• Further hearing is scheduled for January 20, 2027.
Impact: Neutral (Conditional interim relief granted, awaiting final adjudication)

📍 ORDER WIN

LCC PROJECTS: Wins ₹703 Cr EPC water supply order from Gujarat Water Supply and Sewerage Board, including 10 years of O&M.

KPIGREEN: Signs 300 MW wind power PPA with SJVN at ₹3.64/unit for 25 years.

SATTRIX: Receives cybersecurity work orders worth ₹2.43 Cr during October 2026.

📍 ACQUISITION

ARKADE: Acquires 100% stake in Woollen and Textile Industries for ₹145.51 Cr.

NDTV: Completes acquisition of GoodTimes channel after MIB approval for transfer of broadcasting permissions.

📍 COLLABORATION

COFORGE: Launches BridgeCX real-time personalisation solution with Pega and Mastercard Dynamic Yield for AI-powered customer engagement.

📍 LEADERSHIP CHANGES

ALKEM: Appoints Dr. Amrut Naik as CEO and KMP, effective November 11, 2026; brings 26+ years of pharma experience.

TOURISM FINANCE CORPORATION: Appoints Vandana Sinha as Non-Executive Non-Independent Director, subject to shareholder approval.

SKYWAYS: AVP-HR Kamal Kant Virthare resigns effective October 31, 2026.

SDC TECHMEDIA: Independent Director Megha Saraf resigns; Nidhi Jajodia appointed as Additional Director.

📍 NEW PROJECTS

BONDADA: Signs non-binding MoU with Goa government for proposed solar and biogas projects worth approximately ₹3,000 Cr; 700+ jobs expected.

MAGELLANIC CLOUD: UAV manufacturing and testing facility under JV MCRAY XTEND INDIA is ready; commercial operations to begin in phases.

GUJARAT INJECT: Leases two premises at Sanand for factory operations and thermal and renewable energy R&D.

📍 FUNDRAISING

DIAMOND POWER INFRASTRUCTURE: Raises ₹1,613.97 Cr through QIP at ₹227/share; ₹516.19 Cr remains unutilised.

MONEY MASTERS: Board to consider fundraising through preferential issue, QIP, rights issue or other permissible modes on November 6.

📍 Q2 / BUSINESS UPDATE

YATHARTH HOSPITALS: Raises bed expansion target to 7,000–8,000; proposed ₹3,150 Cr Advent investment for 24.9% stake, with Gurugram hospital targeted for H1 FY28.

PRINCE PIPES: Q2 PAT surges 220% YoY to ₹48 Cr; revenue up 38%, volumes up 22% and EBITDA margin at 12.2%.

DIAMOND POWER INFRASTRUCTURE: Q2 PAT surges 349% YoY and revenue rises 135%; borrowings decline to approximately ₹1,975 Cr.

ZYDUS WELLNESS: Q2 revenue rises 73% YoY, EBITDA surges 272% and PAT turns positive; domestic business grows 29.2%.

INDOGULF CROPSCIENCES: Q2 EBITDA rises 27% to ₹41 Cr and PAT up 24% to ₹26 Cr; EBITDA margin expands 300 bps to 15.9%.

MMP INDUSTRIES: Q2 revenue up 35% to ₹252.7 Cr, EBITDA up 44% to ₹19.3 Cr and PAT up 73% to ₹12.1 Cr; 18,000 MTPA wire rod plant targeted in Q4 FY27.

GLOBAL SURFACES: Q2 revenue rises 11% YoY; EBITDA turns positive at ₹1.3 Cr. Domestic dispatches commence, while input and freight costs remain elevated.

RAJESH POWER: H1 revenue up 46% to ₹929 Cr, EBITDA up 33% to ₹112 Cr and PAT up 35% to ₹79 Cr; order book around ₹4,000 Cr.

UMIYA MOBILE: H1 revenue rises 45% to ₹529.49 Cr, EBITDA up 78% to ₹11.32 Cr and PAT up 92% to ₹7.26 Cr.

EPACK PREFAB: Maintains FY27 revenue guidance of ₹1,900–1,950 Cr; order book rises 59% to ₹1,462.5 Cr, with ₹150 Cr capex planned.

JYOTI CNC: Order book reaches ₹5,082 Cr; Q2 dispatches hit record 1,900 machines. Receives ₹1,020.65 Cr ECMS investment approval over five years.

SOLAR INDUSTRIES: Management expects to surpass FY27 guidance; anticipates large defence orders, including potential guided Pinaka rocket orders.

LLOYDS ENGINEERING WORKS: Targets ₹10,000+ Cr revenue by FY30; combined order book exceeds ₹10,355 Cr following acquisitions.

AJMERA REALTY: Expects stronger H2 FY27; reduces debt by ₹34 Cr to ₹646 Cr and continues 5X growth strategy.

INDIGO: CEO Willie Walsh says airline will have 14 narrow-body A321 XLR aircraft by December 2027.

📍 INCORPORATE / CORPORATE STRUCTURE

CAMS: Step-down subsidiary Think Analytics Consultancy Services voluntarily liquidated and dissolved; no business impact.

IZMO: Subsidiary develops indigenous defence-qualified Pitch Detector for military aircraft and helicopters, replacing an imported component.

DIAMOND POWER INFRASTRUCTURE: Approves ₹170 Cr in-principle capex for Vadodara integrated polymer complex to manufacture cable-grade compounds for cables up to 400 kV.

📍 IT NEWS

NSE: NSE International Exchange launches 23.5-hour daily trading from November 2, covering Asian, European and American market sessions.

📍 OTHERS

QUADRANT TELEVENTURES: NCLT Mumbai Bench-I approves resolution plan under IBC on November 3; certified order awaited.

NUVAMA: Upgrades ITC to BUY from HOLD; prefers United Breweries and Radico Khaitan in alcoholic beverages.

KOTAK INSTITUTIONAL EQUITIES: Upgrades Escorts to BUY with target price of ₹3,100.

AIA ENGINEERING: Order book stands at ₹1,071 Cr; installed capacity at 4,36,000 TPA and H1 FY27 capex at ₹86 Cr.

RADHIKA JEWELTECH: Board adopts unaudited financial results for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.

GANESH CONSUMER PRODUCTS: Uploads Q2 FY27 earnings conference call recording.

RM DRIP AND SPRINKLERS: Board meeting scheduled for November 9 to consider Q2 and H1 FY27 results.

AWFIS: Grants 3,116 employee stock options at ₹168.99 each; 2,65,942 options lapsed.

IIFL CAPITAL: Open offer escrow disclosure shows nil shares tendered as of November 3.

**CLSA – LIC HOUSING FINANCE**

**Rating & Target Price**
- Rating: Outperform.
- Target price: ₹620.

**Q2 FY27 Performance**
- NII reported broadly in line with estimates.
- PAT exceeded estimates by 15%.
- Recoveries from written-off accounts aided profitability.
- Negative credit costs supported PAT performance.

**Margins & Lending Rates**
- NIM remained stable QoQ.
- Prime lending rate increased by 25 bps.
- Rate hike should support margins.
- Incremental lending yields remain 70 bps lower.
- Comparison is against overall portfolio yields.

**Loan Growth & Disbursements**
- Disbursement growth improved over three quarters.
- Overall loan growth remains modest at 4–5%.

**Business Strategy**
- Increasing focus on higher-yielding lending segments.
- Loans against property gaining strategic focus.
- Prime housing faces intense bank competition.

**Key Takeaway**
- PAT beat was supported by recoveries.
- Lending rate increase may support margins.
- Loan growth remains relatively subdued.
- LAP focus targets higher lending yields.
- Impact: **Mixed**

**BOFA SECURITIES – ESCORTS KUBOTA DOWNGRADE**

**Rating & Target Price**
- Rating downgraded to Underperform.
- Target price cut to ₹2,100.
- Earlier target price: ₹3,500.

**Q2 FY27 Performance & Margin Pressure**
- Q2 performance missed estimates.
- Margins declined 300 bps QoQ.
- Sharp margin squeeze driven by metal inflation.
- Metals account for 11–12% of net revenue.
- Margin pressure remains unresolved.

**Tractor Industry Outlook**
- Management commentary signals deeper tractor downcycle.
- Expects double-digit decline during H2.
- FY27 growth outlook turns marginally negative.
- Earlier FY27 growth expectation: 4–5%.

**Earnings & Valuation Concerns**
- EPS estimates cut by 11–13%.
- Weak growth and margin pressure drive downgrades.
- Further valuation downside remains possible.
- Stock valuations remain unattractive versus peers.

**Key Takeaway**
- BOFA sees worsening tractor industry conditions.
- Metal inflation continues pressuring margins.
- Earnings estimates face significant downward revisions.
- Valuation concerns reinforce the downgrade.
- Impact: **Negative**

NALCO – RECORD H1 FY27 FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE

H1 FY27 Financial Highlights
- Total income: ₹11,143 Cr, up 33% YoY.
- EBITDA: ₹5,539 Cr, up 50% YoY.
- PBT: ₹5,160 Cr, up 55% YoY.
- PAT: ₹3,837 Cr, up 54% YoY.
- All figures represent record H1 performance.

Q2 FY27 Performance
- Total income: ₹5,419 Cr, up 26% YoY.
- Net profit: ₹1,835 Cr, up 28% YoY.

Operational Performance
- Record H1 aluminium cast metal production.
- Production reached 2.35 lakh tonnes.
- Highest-ever cumulative domestic alumina sales.
- Highest-ever cumulative domestic metal sales.

Dividend Announcement
- Interim dividend: ₹4.50 per share.
- Dividend payout: ₹826.48 Cr.
- Represents 90% of face value.

Expansion & Growth Plans
- Fifth-stream alumina refinery expansion nearing commissioning.
- 0.5 MTPA brownfield smelter expansion progressing.
- Project location: Angul, Odisha.

Management Commentary
- Strong operational efficiency supported performance.
- Favourable market conditions aided growth.
- Prudent marketing strategies supported financial performance.

Key Takeaway
- Record H1 financial and operational performance.
- Strong profitability growth across key parameters.
- Expansion projects support long-term capacity growth.
- Impact: Positive

Curious when FII will come back to India

So gave Co-pilot a prompt
“Why FIIs wont return to India even as AI trade unwind globally”

Reverse Psychology

Here is the response

1. India is still expensive vs EM peers
o Even after corrections, India trades at a premium to most emerging markets.
o FIIs compare India with China, Korea, Taiwan, Brazil, not with India's own history.
o If China is at 10-12x PE and India at 20-25x PE, capital tends to chase cheaper markets. 
2. India lacks direct AI beneficiaries
o The AI trade created winners in US tech, Taiwan semiconductors and Korean memory-chip companies.
o India has very few large listed AI, semiconductor or hyperscaler plays that global thematic funds can buy. 
3. Dollar returns matter, not rupee returns
o FIIs think in USD.
o Even if Nifty is flat or slightly up, rupee depreciation can wipe out returns.
o Currency risk remains a major deterrent for foreign capital. 
4. US yields remain a strong competitor
o If US Treasuries offer attractive risk-free returns, FIIs need a much higher expected return from India.
o Many global allocators prefer earning 4-5% in dollar assets rather than taking EM risk. 
5. India's earnings growth has moderated
o India's premium valuation was justified when earnings were compounding rapidly.
o If earnings growth slows while valuations remain rich, FIIs question the risk-reward. 
6. Better opportunities elsewhere
o Korea, Taiwan and China offer exposure to AI, semiconductors and manufacturing at lower valuations.
o Global funds have finite capital; India is competing against these markets for allocation. 
7. India is no longer an under-owned market
o After years of strong inflows, most EM funds already have meaningful India exposure.
o Incremental flows require a new catalyst, not just the absence of AI enthusiasm.
8. Domestic flows reduce urgency
o SIPs, mutual funds and insurance money continue supporting Indian markets despite FII selling.
o Paradoxically, this resilience prevents large valuation corrections that would otherwise attract FIIs back.

Maruti Suzuki India should be rechristened as Suzuki India

Maruti's journey started as a Govt of India project. Maruti Udyog was the Indian promoter & Suzuki was brought in as the technology partner. Back then, this was very much an Indian company with Japanese know-how.

Over time, the Indian promoter gradually diluted its holding & eventually exited completely. Suzuki did the opposite, staying invested through every cycle & steadily increasing its stake.

What began as a JV slowly became Suzuki's most important global asset. The ownership story itself tells you who has deepened commitment over the decades.

For years, investors debated why Suzuki was setting up fresh manufacturing capacity outside Maruti Suzuki through its Gujarat subsidiary instead of housing it directly in the listed entity.

Then came the reversal. Suzuki transferred Suzuki Motor Gujarat into Maruti Suzuki at a valuation of roughly ₹12,000+ Cr. Rather than taking cash, it largely took equity.

The result? Suzuki's ownership in Maruti Suzuki moved up further without having to buy equivalent shares from the secondary market.

This wasn't just a restructuring exercise. It was Suzuki effectively converting manufacturing assets into a larger stake in India's largest PV company.

Even after that transaction, Suzuki did not stop. It has periodically picked up additional shares from the open market whenever opportunities emerged.

The message is clear. The Indian promoter exited long ago. The Japanese promoter keeps doubling down on India.

Look at the cars on the road today. The branding emphasis is on the giant "S" logo. 10-15years back, cars started selling with only “S” logo, 1st on premium nexa cars, then on all the models. You will hardly see Maruti branded cars on road now

For many younger buyers, the brand recall is shifting from "Maruti Suzuki" to simply "Suzuki". The transition is subtle but visible.

India is now the crown jewel of Suzuki Motor Corp. A substantial portion of Suzuki valuation come from Indian listed entity. Maruti $38bn mcap translate to $21bn (for 58% stake, $15bn if applied 30% Holdco disc).

Even beyond that, Maruti pays over $500m to Suzuki as royalty, that value must be over $5bn in the SoTP of Suzuki motors. Suzuki motors also have successful 2w biz in India, they are 6th largest 2w in India, clocking over 1lac units every month

In many ways, investors buying Suzuki Motor Corp are indirectly buying the India story. Cars sold by Suzuki in India is higher than overall car sold by Suzuki in other 100 countries combined

A rebranding to "Suzuki India" could also help shed the old "cheap small-car company" perception. As premium SUVs, hybrids & future EVs gain share, a stronger global MNC identity may command a different customer mindset.

Ownership, capital allocation, manufacturing integration, branding & growth strategy all point in one direction: this is increasingly Suzuki's India story.

Conclusion: Maruti only stays in Co. name hence should be renamed now
